title: the import sieve names a module from a slash-keyed path on every platform
intention: import_sieve reads its '/'-keyed import graph the same way on every platform: module_name and the device_isolation rule split graph paths on '/', so on Windows reaches() and the RULE 1 device check measure the real graph instead of an empty one. A walk that resolves none of its own imports is loud, never green.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 by akiendell_cc_0 on akiendell (Windows): import_sieve.module_name (sieve.py:280) splits on os.sep while the graph keys are '/'-normalised (sieve.py:182), so reaches() is empty for every start and every sieve built on it (fire_path_unreachable, the reach sieves) reads green by vacuity there. Read on akienasus at main: sieve.py:586 and :593 (device_isolation, RULE 1's device-path check) split the same graph paths on os.sep, so on Windows no device is found and the encapsulation check reads green by vacuity too.
traces_to: Law 9 (green is earned: a green by vacuity is a false green); RULE 1 (the device-path check must measure on every box); Law 8 (a peer leans on a green).
how: module_name folds backslashes to '/' and splits on '/'; the two device_isolation splits (sieve.py:586, :593) split on '/'; reaches() raises HollowScan when its graph has at least 20 in-tree imports and none resolves to a file, so a vacuous walk is loud. A new proof, one tooth per clause.

clauses.claim: module_name gives the same module for a '/' spelling and a backslash spelling of one path, and the device_isolation split reads '/'-keyed graph paths the same on every platform
reaches() over the real tree is non-empty for a known start
a walk over a graph with at least 20 in-tree imports, none of which resolves to a file, raises HollowScan instead of reading green; a single dead import stays quiet

decisions.text: D1: module_name and the device_isolation splits read '/'; reaches() raises HollowScan over a graph that resolves none of at least 20 in-tree imports.
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause.

out: the import graph's key format (sieve.py:182 stays)

measured.saw: reaches() empty for every start on Windows; every sieve on it green by vacuity

measured.saw: sieve.py:280, :586, :593 split graph paths on os.sep; :182 normalises keys to '/'
